focus: Phase 2 materials: statue rendering via PawnRenderer.SetStatue on a live pawn (side effects), material stage stats (are StatDefOf members and MarketValue/MeleeDamageFactor offsets actually applied to pawns), the 5 new Harmony patches, inheritance and save/load of material
diffSource: since build 13 (2026-10-06T01:54:55Z), the last reviewed build, from the build log

findings.title: MarketValue stat offset in the material stage is never applied to pawns, but the tooltip shows it
findings.detail: For a pawn, StatWorker_MarketValue.GetValueUnfinalized calls base.GetValueUnfinalized(StatRequest.For(req.BuildableDef, req.StuffDef)). That request has no Thing, so StatWorker's hediff statOffsets loop never sees the pawn. The only hediff input is PriceUtility.PawnQualityPriceOffset, which reads def.priceOffset/priceImpact and not the stage. The 'worth its jade' offset in TitanMaterialUtility.BuildStage does nothing. HediffStatsUtility.SpecialDisplayStats(MaterialStage) still lists it in the Hediff_Titan tooltip, so players see a value bonus they don't get. The modifier also calls ButcherCount → GenMath.RoundRandom, so building the stage (which can happen from a tooltip) consumes Rand. Remove the MarketValue StatModifier from BuildStage. If the price bonus is wanted, add it some other way, for example a StatPart on MarketValue.

findings.title: Becoming a construct keeps existing requiresFlesh traits
findings.detail: TitanUtility.CanAddTrait refuses requiresFlesh traits on a construct (TitanUtility.cs:66). SetMaterialInternal only swaps the material extension's own traits and never removes flesh-only traits the titan already had. A flesh titan with a flesh trait that later gets SetMaterial/RollMaterial (including the debug action, and the inheritance path at TitanUtility.cs:152) ends up as a stone creature with a trait the framework says it can't have. In SetMaterialInternal, when stuff != null, remove the traits whose def.requiresFlesh is set.

findings.title: Material trait swap removes traits the creature rolled on its own and adds traits without checking conflicts
findings.detail: On a material change, every trait in the old material's extension is removed (unless the new material has it too), even if the creature rolled that trait independently before. New material traits go through AddTraitInternal directly, so ConflictsWith exclusions are never checked. Recording which traits came from the material (a flag on TitanTrait) would let the swap remove only those.

findings.title: IsLiveTitan calls GetTitan, which can remove from the registry, on vanilla's parallel pre-draw threads
findings.detail: PawnRenderNodeWorker_TitanOverlay.CanDrawNow now calls TitanVisualsUtility.IsLiveTitan, which calls TitanUtility.GetTitan. When the registered hediff is no longer in the hediff set, GetTitan runs Unregister(pawn), which is registry.Remove (TitanUtility.cs:36-42). Vanilla builds draw requests inside DynamicDrawManager's IJobParallelFor PreDrawThings (DynamicDrawManager.cs:129-140, DrawPhase.ParallelPreDraw), so two worker threads can remove from the same Dictionary at once. It only happens for stale entries, but a corrupted Dictionary throws or hangs. In IsLiveTitan, look the hediff up without side effects, e.g. parms.pawn.health.hediffSet.GetFirstHediff<Hediff_Titan>()?.IsConstruct, or call a read-only TryGetValue that never unregisters.

findings.title: SetMaterial leaves existing requiresFlesh traits on a pawn that becomes a construct
findings.detail: CanAddTrait now refuses requiresFlesh traits on a construct (TitanUtility.cs:66), but SetMaterial / SetMaterialInternal only swaps the material's own extension traits (Hediff_Titan.cs:80-95). Calling SetMaterial or RollMaterial on an existing flesh titan therefore produces a stone creature that keeps its flesh traits, the state the new check is meant to prevent. In SetMaterial, when stuff != null, remove the traits whose def.requiresFlesh is true before or after SetMaterialInternal. Inheritance avoids this only because the material is set before any trait is added.

findings.title: Statue flag on a live pawn turns off the damage flash and the humanlike render cache
findings.detail: SetStatue only sets statueStuff, and the rest of the game reads it only for drawing. Three side effects: (1) PawnRenderNodeWorker.GetMaterialPropertyBlock uses parms.statueColor instead of parms.tint, so the red damage flash no longer shows; (2) PawnRenderer.GetDrawParms sets useCached=false whenever the Statue flag is set, so humanlike constructs are drawn uncached every frame; (3) skin shaders (HeadTypeDef.cs:37, PawnRenderNode.ShaderFor) and apparel graphics switch to their statue versions. Nothing breaks. Worth knowing for performance with many humanlike constructs.

findings.title: Blood prefixes return bool (lint prefix-returns-void)
findings.detail: The DropBloodFilth and DropBloodSmear prefixes return false to skip the original. No mod among the 15 scanned corpus trees patches either method, so nothing is disabled today. The blood def comes from RaceProps (Pawn_HealthTracker.cs:1359), so there is no clean void-prefix alternative. Keep them, but expect the lint to flag them.

findings.title: A removed stuff def silently turns a construct back into flesh and leaves its material traits
findings.detail: Scribe_Defs.Look(ref material) loads null if the stuff's mod is removed. The material-granted traits are saved in the traits list, so they stay while IsConstruct turns false. Harmless, but PostLoadInit could log it once.

findings.title: Statue flag on a live humanlike turns off the vanilla render cache
findings.detail: PawnRenderer sets useCached = false whenever PawnRenderFlags.Statue is set. Every humanlike material titan is drawn node by node every frame instead of from the cached texture at normal zoom. This is fine for a few pawns but worth knowing if constructs are common (for example, a whole faction of them).

findings.title: The statue is only reapplied after loading if the race has a render tree
findings.detail: ApplyStatue(dirty:false) runs only from DynamicPawnRenderNodeSetup_Titan.GetDynamicNodes. PawnRenderTree.TrySetupGraphIfNeeded returns before SetupDynamicNodes when RaceProps.renderTree.root.nodeClass is null, so for such a race the renderer field is never set again after a load. Rare; calling ApplyStatue once from ExposeData's PostLoadInit (or SpawnSetup) would cover it.

findings.title: A material trait can be inherited from the parent whose material the child didn't get
findings.detail: Count() collects every heritable trait from both parents, including traits that come from a parent's TitanMaterialExtension. A child that gets the father's wood can still inherit the mother's granite trait as a free-standing trait, and a later SetMaterialInternal won't remove it because it is not in the new material's old-traits list. Skipping traits that belong to either parent's material extension in Count() would keep material traits tied to the material. Whether this is intended is a design call.
